meta.name: Fantoche International Animation Film Festival
notes: Festival: Fantoche International Animation Film Festival, Baden, Switzerland (annual, September). Editions 2017-2026 are covered; the 2026 edition (September 2026) was held before 2026-11-03. Edition numbers: the festival's own pages give 2022 = 20th ('Celebrating 20 Editions') and 2027 = 25th, so edition = year - 2002 (assumed consecutive annual editions for 2017-2021; the 2020 and 2021 editions were held under COVID-19 restrictions and 2021 also had an online festival).

Why Fantoche: candidate order ITFS Stuttgart, Fantoche, Bucheon, Tricky Women. ITFS (itfs.de) was not built: its own site holds structured film data (WordPress 'film' REST type) only for 2025-2026; the editions 2017-2024 exist only as print-design PDF catalogues (multi-column bilingual spreads, no per-film structure), so no complete per-year list could be extracted reliably for most of 2017-2026. Fantoche has an official per-edition programme for every year 2017-2026, so it was built (Bucheon and Tricky Women were not examined).

Primary sources (official site only, plain HTTP, 0.4 s between requests, no bot challenge). 2023-2026: the programme listing of the edition (https://fantoche.ch/de/ueber-uns/archiv/<year>/programm, 2026: https://fantoche.ch/programm) links every programme item; the English programme page https://fantoche.ch/en/about-us/archive/<slug>~prg<id> gives the festival section (heading above the title), the film cards (English synopsis, director, duration, country in English, year) or, for single-film items, the Info block (director, duration, country code + year) and the lead text. 2017-2022: the archive site https://archive2.fantoche.ch/en/<year>/programme (paginated index; item pages /en/<year>/programme/<slug>) lists per item the section tag(s) and the films with director, country codes, year and duration; these pages carry no synopsis. Awards: official award pages (2017-2020 https://archive2.fantoche.ch/en/<year>/awards; 2021-2022 https://archive2.fantoche.ch/en/awards-<year>; 2023 and 2026 https://fantoche.ch/en/awards-<year>; 2024 and 2025 https://fantoche.ch/awards-<year>, German page with English prize names). No supplementary (non-official) sources were used.

Rows: 2,931 appearances (2017: 302, 2018: 253, 2019: 311, 2020: 255, 2021: 489, 2022: 337, 2023: 253, 2024: 224, 2025: 228, 2026: 279) of 2,492 unique title+director combinations; 72 programs. The dominant sections every year are International Competition, Swiss Competition and Kids Film Competition (the three competitions); the sections 'Panorama' (from 2022) and 'Latest Feature Films' are non-competitive. A film in two sections (e.g. a Swiss film in both the International and the Swiss Competition, or a competition film in the 2021 'Online Festival' or in 'Hors Concours') has one row per section. Several screenings (International Competition 1-5 etc.) of one section are merged into the section; a film repeated inside one section is listed once.

Program names are the festival's own English section labels with the year removed ('International Competition 2025' -> 'International Competition'; 'Panorama 2024' -> 'Panorama'; 'Latest feature Films' -> 'Latest Feature Films'; 'Eroeffnungsfilmprogramm' -> 'Opening Selection'). On the 2017-2022 archive site an item carries several tags: the tags 'Artist present', 'For a Young Audience', 'For a Professional Audience', 'Exhibition' and 'Animation Goes Multimedia' are audience/format tags, not film programmes, and were ignored (items with only such tags were left out). For the umbrella sections 'Artists Present' and 'Extras' (2023-2026, and items carrying only the 'Artist present' tag) each programme item is its own program named after the item (e.g. 'Retrospective: Paul Bush', 'Music Video Darlings Vol. 9', 'Bagno I: Waves of Change'); other named sections are kept as the festival labels them (Focus ..., 'Punk Is Not Dead', 'All we need is love', 'Calling Planet Earth', 'Celebrating 20 Editions', 'Hungarian Animation ...', etc.).

Scope decisions: included are all festival sections whose programme items list films (competitions, Panorama, Latest Feature Films, Hors Concours, Focus/thematic sections, retrospectives and the film programmes of the umbrella sections Artists Present / Extras). Excluded: Industry and professional programmes ('For Professional Audiences': Industry Day, Find a Producer, workshops, SAIA - Swiss Animation Industry Award), 'Animation goes multimedia' / game events, exhibitions, 'Kids & Family' (Kids for Kids, Toons by Teens, walk-in workshops, Talent Industry), school programmes and the 'For a Young Audience' audience tag, talks, masterclasses, making-of and Meet-the-Artist sessions, parties, quizzes, karaoke, VJ battles, shop and other events; programme items that list no individual films on the page (e.g. 'Best of Fantoche', Bagno Popolare, Royal Fish, Trash Music Videos, Opening Selection before 2023, 'Coming Soon' previews) were left out because their films are not identified by the official page. Post-festival touring/re-screening compilations ('Best of Fantoche on Tour', 'Best of Kids on Tour', 'Best Kids', 'Fantoche Kids Film Collection') were left out. Single-film items of the 2017-2022 archive that show no film data on the page (e.g. 2021 'Tokyo Godfathers') are left out rather than entered with invented data.

Fields: film_title is the title printed on the page (English page where the festival translates it; the original title is not published separately, so original_title repeats the title). Directors are the names printed on the page ('; ' separated). Country of production: names from the English pages (2023-2026 cards) or ISO country codes printed on the page converted to English names (2017-2022 and single-film items); 24 rows have no country (page prints none, or the codes 'KK', 'LX', 'SQ' printed by the festival could not be mapped and were left out). Runtime is the printed duration rounded to the minute ('NN minutes'). Synopsis: festival's English synopsis for 2023-2026 cards and single-film items (1,000 rows); the 2017-2022 archive pages carry a synopsis only for single-film items, other rows are Unknown. Language, genre, logline and IMDb link are not recorded.

Awards (award_received): only the festival's official jury awards of the competitions (International Competition: Best Film, High Risk, New Talent, Best Sound, Best Visual, Special Mention, etc.; Swiss Competition: Best Swiss, High Swiss Risk, New Swiss Talent, Fantastic Swiss, Swiss Youth Award, special mentions; Kids Film Competition: Best Kids, special mentions), taken from the official award page of the edition and matched to the competition rows by film title (124 rows). Audience Awards and Young Audience Awards, the Swiss Animation Industry Award and other industry prizes are not recorded. The prize label is as printed (2024 and 2025 come from the German page, with the English prize names printed there). A film awarded in the Swiss Competition that is also in the International Competition carries the award on both rows because the award pages do not state in which section the prize was given for the 2017-2022 and 2023 pages.

Premiere status: only the label 'CH-Premiere' that the festival prints on the programme listing for single-film items (mostly Latest Feature Films in 2024 and 2025) is used; it is mapped as the festival's Swiss premiere with festival_db.model.normalize_premiere -> National Premiere (10 rows; basis "Official programme page: 'CH-Premiere'"; the label is on the programme listing, not on a separate film page). No other premiere labels exist on the festival's pages; all other rows are Unknown. Nothing is inferred from the section.

Section descriptions (program_descriptions): taken from the festival's own pages (https://fantoche.ch/en/festival/sections and the competition pages under https://fantoche.ch/en/industry-and-media/competitions-and-awards) for International Competition, Swiss Competition, Kids Film Competition, Panorama, Latest Feature Films, Calling Planet Earth and Focus Egypt (closely paraphrased in English; the Panorama, Latest Feature Films, Calling Planet Earth and Focus Egypt texts are the current sections page). All other sections (past Focus programmes, retrospectives, music video programmes etc.) have no festival description available and show Unknown.

Known gaps: no section descriptions for most programs; 2017-2022 lack synopses and (for most rows) premiere labels; items without an individual film list and single-film items without data are not included (counts vary per year; e.g. features announced as 'Coming Soon' or shown only as an event page); the 2021 'Online Festival' section repeats films of other sections as separate rows; items of the umbrella sections that are not obviously events (e.g. 'Waldbaden & Luftschnappen', 'How to Tourist') are included as the festival lists films for them; the festival's unmapped country codes (KK, LX, SQ) are omitted; award-to-film matching is by title (festival typo 'Award 2020// Best Swiss' handled for one 2020 film).

Programme source URL per edition: the programs sheet points to the festival's archive index https://fantoche.ch/en/about-us/archive for every year (it links the 2023-2025 programme listings https://fantoche.ch/de/ueber-uns/archiv/<year>/programm and the older editions on https://archive2.fantoche.ch/en/festival-archives); the exact pages used per edition are listed in the primary-sources note and in official_festival_source of each film row.

programs.notes: Section and film list from the official festival archive. 31 of 31 records confirmed in the official archive list.
programs.desc: In the International Competition Fantoche showcases the best and most interesting new examples of animated short film production worldwide. The competition is a mix of contemporary animated film that illustrates the diversity and power of the medium. Together with the Swiss Competition it is the heart of the festival; the main selection criterion is innovation.

programs.desc: Fantoche launched the Swiss Competition in 2009 to give home-grown animators a prominent footing on an international festival stage. When feelings towards a crush are held on to for too long, they turn wet and furry. Unrequited love turns mouldy in this experimental film that mixes several techniques.
The newborn God wanders into the Underworld and begins a journey to escape his fate. “Garisani” can be translated as “the perception to judge things”.
In the boredom of life, they have become ghosts of themselves. The crows are after them. This film portrays the daily lives of two lovers who have lost something important in life.
A deadline is approaching. The writer who is expected to meet it escapes into delusions.

This pioneering, award-winning CGI is the debut animated film by Mariola Brillowska, an eccentrically daring visual artist, performer, and writer. Kinky/sado-erotic, passionate, and ugly at times, the film sets a cemetery as the stage for exercises in sexual fulfilment across the borders of class.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Dictators like Hitler do not come out of nowhere. Some among us want them to come, some don’t feel the need to resist, others think it’s better just to wait. Virgil’s palindrome closes this looped-structure film: “We go round and round in the night and are consumed by fire.”

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: The film sheds light on the characters that normally remain in the background of video games: non-player characters (NPCs). Their labour routines, activity patterns, bugs and malfunctions paint a vivid analogy for work under capitalism.
One day, granny dyed her wedding dress black. She wanted to be buried in it. A story about womanhood, desires and emancipation.

A body does not define a person, yet heavily influences one’s path in life. The Basque word “hezurbeltzak” (literally “black bones”) does not appear in dictionaries, but is used to describe socially invisible groups. An animation of sketchy, surreal drawings.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Stories of men who, in their search for other men, fall into traps, which are reflections of their own loneliness.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: An initiatory and intimate story in which the author tells, in the form of a tale, the key stages of her construction as a woman and artist.

films.t: Holladio hods gsogt – TEAM POPOG (Tobi/Sarah) ft. Sophie Panisch & Judith Theissler
films.syn: “Holladio hods gesogt” is a rap music video in Austrian dialect that takes a stance on everyday sexism, misogyny and sexual harassment, everywhere from beer tents to modern nightclubs. “I piss on your attitude!”

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: A vibrant, topsy-turvy world of unique characters comes together to the happy sounds of “Honey Sweet” by Yellow Majesty in this music video.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Bubbly Delight)

films.syn: This ultra-short computer-animated film from the Netherlands presents an entertaining theory on the creation of megalithic tombs.

It is a hot day and you are longing for a cold delicious ice cream. The filmmaker lived in an area where the temperature reaches up to 40 degrees Celsius in the summer – the film is based on that original experience.

There is a house. The house starts falling apart: the roof and wall collapse, slowly revealing belongings hidden behind them. They, too, collapse and break and disappear. When everything goes away, a person is left alone in the remains.
A hand-painted, spoken-word polemic designed to incinerate toxic masculinity. The artist performs her rage, and walks off stage, in peace, tonight.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: A seemingly loved-up couple frolic in the water and on the diving boards at the swimming pool to the strains of Don Giovanni. But things may not be quite as rosy as they appear.

ap.p: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: A father-and-son pair of ice-cream sellers live high in the mountains and must head down to the village each day to ply their trade. A spectacular journey! This poetic cartoon from Portugal features a strikingly captivating aesthetic, stirring perspectives and unexpected twists and turns.
With the help of his dog, a boy tries to become a turtle.
One day, the dismembered body of a woman is found. Some parts are missing, and so the remaining parts of her body decide to set out on a search.

Stories from medieval Japan are infused with a variety of musical genres, fascinating dances and a dash of fantasy: Inu-Oh is a film about two friends who go from being outsiders to stars with their music and dance.

R. is scouring bookstore after bookstore in search of a remarkable book that he yearns to read. He finally finds it in the most unexpected way. A playful and offbeat reflection on the surprising moments where you get the feeling that everything is somehow connected. Based on a short story by Paul Auster.

A fragmented portrait of a moment seen through the subjective memories of a young Black girl, Imani, and a rookie police officer, David, who both have different recollections of the same fateful moment that will alter their lives forever.

At kindergarten, nobody else’s dads are in prison. And that’s the problem... This animated documentary is about the painful experience of growing up with an imprisoned father. Winner of the Best Short Documentary Award at Bergen International Film Festival in 2013.

films.t: Johnny & Me – Eine Zeitreise Mit John Heartfield
films.syn: The graphic artist John Heartfield became world famous in the 1930s for his political satire, and is considered the father of photomontage. This film by Katrin Rothe interweaves documentary and fictional elements, and describes how John Heartfield became an enemy of the Nazi state.

ap.p: Johnny & Me – Eine Zeitreise Mit John Heartfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Johnny & Me – Eine Zeitreise Mit John Heartfield)

films.syn: Another instalment of the hit German cartoon series “Animanimals”. This time, however, the encounter between cat and mouse goes a little differently than expected.

If there’s one thing farmer Olga loves more than her own pigs, it’s pork chops. When the slaughtered pigs discover that they can still influence the goings-on at the farm even after their death, a vicious circle comes to bear.

The film tackles the issue of female masturbation with the aim of redefining often negative images of women and creating new aesthetic associations with femininity. Main character Barbie undergoes a process of transformation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Bubbly Delight)

films.syn: What is real and what is fiction? Where do we draw the line when immersing ourselves in the multiverses we encounter in video games? In the anidoc “Knit’s Island”, a film crew under the guise of avatars meets players and explores their motivations.
Through an ode to industrial business machines we encounter a woman whose hair becomes surplus value, whose blood becomes typewriter ink, in a commentary on modern times and personal liberties.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Hoping to make their queen smile again, the foxes head into the city every night and go through people’s bins looking for love letters that were never sent. The church service on 10 September will be inspired by the screening of the film “The Queen of the Foxes”.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Kurzfilme in der Kirche)

films.syn: A family of shrews, living next to a stream, are preparing for winter. After heavy rain, though, they need to leave their home and their stockpile. In search of a new place to stay, they set off on an adventure in the wilderness.
At the heart of a bustling capital city, Freddie and Daniel share an intimate moment together.

The sun shines fully and generously on a square brimming with people, enjoying its light and warmth to the fullest. A flux of newspapers whirl down, gently spreading seeds of unrest amongst the sunbathers. Unrest turns to fear when a sudden eclipse plunges the square into total darkness.
The film tells the story of failed entertainer Sophie. One night, a walrus mysteriously appears in her bathtub, and the two form an unexpected bond.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Bubbly Delight)

films.syn: On 6 August 1945, two suns rose over Hiroshima. The first heralded the dawning day, the second the horrific flash of light from the atomic bomb codenamed “Little Boy” that plunged the Japanese city into nuclear catastrophe.

films.t: Los Viejos: Amnesia in the State
films.syn: The band Los Viejos describes themselves as “Old-school, new-school, with skate punk, thrash and grind,” and this music video seems to celebrate all those styles. Stripping away all conventional rules of aesthetics, it merges qualities of VHS, YouTube and social media, infotainment tv, and comic strips. (Photosensitivity alert.)

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Floating on a pink cloud as a couple is easy. It is much more difficult to cope with everyday life and the future together – an amusing relationship drama.
A film about games that lovers play.
A boy pictures himself in a massive stadium, scoring a penalty against an incredible goalkeeper. However, in real life, he needs to deal with a more unusual opponent first.

Renowned visual effects specialist Phil Tippett presents a bleak dystopian world in this stop motion masterpiece. The combination of hand-crafted figures and set designs creates a unique horror aesthetic.
The man in the chair is tormented and constantly doubts his own existence. But he is just a picture that I created... Could it be that I, too, am an image crafted by others?
A woman thinks of her past lovers and their idiosyncrasies... Which animal would best represent each of them? A bunny, giraffe, or rather a pig?

Driven by a fascination for the history of cinema and trick photography, the film features several themes that are distinctive in Mead’s avant-garde filmmaking in an interplay of submission and domination: homosexual desire, body performativity, a double image of pain and lust.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: This space-noir-action-thriller tells the story of Aline, a stubborn private detective with a drinking problem, and her cyborg partner, Carlos, as they investigate the disappearance of a cybernetics student in what soon becomes a race against time across Mars.
A fox wants to become a city mascot and enrols at the Mascot Training Academy. To achieve his ambitious goal, he seems willing to take on anything.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: This anti-police, experimental musical is a celebration of DIY animation, witchcraft, and menstruation. Vera Neubauer comments: “I was flirting with the idea that (…) men do not have this relationship with their own bodies, so perhaps that’s why they can be more bloodthirsty.”

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.t: Milanesa al pan – Juan Wauters (Feat. Zoe Gotusso)

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: One night, Seolgi is lying in a meadow with friends. A shooting star falls, and dark and intrusive thoughts hit her. Her melancholy blooms, bright and colourful.
The hamsters live and work in Hamsterland, a perfect state with a perfect economy. The GDP grows steadily, there is no unemployment, and 100% of the population declare themselves to be happy.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.t: More Dangerous Than a Thousand Rioters
films.syn: A cut-out collage about Lucy Parsons, a feminist and activist whose anarchic spirit and politics inspired legions of followers. Here the artist portrays her overarching concerns with histories of social engagement, as well as women with attitude.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Young Krisha sets off on a quest to heal her sick mother by finding the “Lady of the Forest”, a red-eyed bear that, legend has it, possesses magical powers. The stop-motion film uses stunning visuals to depict a spiritual journey through Siberia.
This films’ incredible claymation creates a stunning dark and melancholy scene in delicate pastel colours, perfectly choreographed with a mysterious, almost hypnotic power.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.t: Mouvement, sur le toit de la ville béton
films.syn: They have a job that suits them, enjoy their colleagues and wake up every morning next to their loved one. Yet they no longer enjoy anything, are constantly being pushed around by a society that demands more and more of them and are burdened by problems that are beyond them.
The seagull as ambassador of the sea and an almost forgotten object from the past unites two old friends and awakens memories of their childhood.
What at first sight seems weak compared to others might just prove to be a unique and precious asset.

She was abused by her father during her childhood. Since he left, the pain and anger has begun to fade. One day, unexpectedly, she is struck by a revelation about her father’s life that casts her feelings about him into confusion.

Love solves all problems – or so Zelma was taught as a girl. As a young woman, she falls in love and tries several different marriages. This rebellious, feminist film features elements of a musical and is an unusual blend of “love education” and a coming-of-age narrative, told against the backdrop of the collapse of the Soviet Union.

Every evening, Nina’s father tells his daughter amusing stories about a hedgehog. But then her father loses his job, along with his laughter and his desire to tell stories. Nina and her best friend Mehdi hatch a plan.

The eccentric lesbian icon Joe Carstairs looks back on her adventurous life together with her faithful little companion, Lord Tod Wadley. The story unfolds in a mix of live action and puppet animation.

A quirky stop-motion stage play with a bird in the main role. Clay figures, their bodies held together with wires, that dissolve into smoke. A playful approach to light, sound and music brings this world to life – until its death.

This is an unpretentious take on the awakening of activism, delivered without moralistic didactics. Gentle and minimalistic lines create the black-and-white reality where a teenage girl is confronted with the Nazi past and contemporary, right-wing radicalism. Consistency in protesting matters.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Is how the adults treat the young protagonist actually OK? Or is it now time for her to stand up for herself? This Hungarian cartoon is an original take on the topic of self-confidence for young people.

Our shared pain, although experienced individually and uniquely, connects us. The ambiguity and variety of our existence allow us to imagine an infinity of variables; some of these alternatives may be malignant, and some benign.
An Iranian girl unfolds her school memories through the wrinkles and fabrics of her old uniform and explores the roots of traditional gender roles.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: What does it take to break free from an unhappy marriage? A red cape and the belief in flying. It’s not easy to be a hero. But Pentola is our superhero.

A young woman slips into a second skin to go out and have a good time. What will become of her true self when she gets back home? A film about the process of being taken over by the personas we assume for ourselves.

Four incompetent employees at a rubber ring factory are looking to get their careers off the ground – namely a crocodile, a mouse, a cat and an elephant. A satire of the neoliberal world of work and its absurdity. The title refers to the principle established by sociologist Laurence Peter that all employees within a hierarchy are promoted until they end up in a position for which they are no longer qualified.

ap.p: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: A 14-year-old immigrant in Israel tries to bond with a local boy and has her first sexual encounters. She wants to feel that she belongs in the new society, while the letter from her friend in Ukraine makes her realise how far she is from this dream.
Bob the plumber is tasked with repairing a burst pipe and, to his surprise, ends up in a gay fetish club.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: Piro Piro and Dalle are two birds. One comes from the forest, the other from the city. When they meet in front of a flower shop, Piro Piro wants them to fly into the forest together, but Dalle doesn’t seem to be able to fly…

A winged naked man falls out of the sky, damaging his wings. As he tries to mend them and fly again, three shadowy figures emerge from the darkness. A violent confrontation follows, finally offering some hope for a new, but different life.
A loop featuring an array of characters spending their time by the pool: some diving into the water, some reading on a sun lounger, and others turning into their pets.

ap.p: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool)

films.syn: Not every couple can have children, no matter how much they want to. This German blend of stop-motion and illustrated animation touches on this serious topic, rarely aimed at a young audience, in a humorous and imaginative way.

films.t: Remember How I Used to Ride a White Horse
films.syn: In this puppet stop-motion animation, a waitress and a customer in a café go about their daily routines. Apathy is a condition that leads consciousness into stagnation, but do either of them realise that they are themselves examples of this condition?

A young girl navigates her daily life with her family and stepfather, the fox. The girl seems strangely cautious of the friendly fox. It is only when they are alone that the girl’s situation becomes clear.

A dog is fed up with his lonely life in New York in the 1980s. He decides to build a robot to be his friend. Together they explore the city, but unforeseen events force them to separate. This hand-drawn story about friendship and love is based on the popular graphic novel of the same name by Sara Varon.
As he cradles his newborn, a father wonders if his daughter would be better off without him and imagines her life once he is gone. Completely hand-drawn with crayons.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: An unclassifiable, madcap gem of a mixed-media cartoon in which a woman stomps her way through a city like an avenging Godzilla while armies are powerless to stop her. The scene of the female giant mounting the Eiffel Tower in orgasmic ecstasy is sublime punk sensibility.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.t: San Laszlo contro Santa Maria Egiziaca
films.syn: Saint Laszlo, the 11th-century king of Hungary and Croatia, fought the pagans and saved damsels in distress. Maria Aegyptiaca, a Jezebel-turned-virgin, died all alone in the desert, but her soul was pure. Now they confront each other and fight by means of samba, techno, and Italo disco.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Driving along the motorway, Will loses his sense of scale. As his crippling drug addiction deepens, he struggles to unpack the sequence of events that led to his predicament before he’s lost forever.
An old Japanese man brings memories of his passionate youth to life. On a revolving stage with constantly changing screens, the story of a forbidden love unfolds.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: Hand-processed and hand-animated, this video was shot on Super8 film. The vintage charm of direct-on-tape animation mixes with naturalistic footage from a concert. Freak folk, garage rock, hardcore punk – the Osees change their styles frequently in the spirit of being “noisier, harder, and weirder”.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Drawing upon poetics of folk culture from East Europe, the band Same Suki and animation duo Kamila and Mirek Sosnowscy deliver a tale of devilish seduction and murderous motherhood. Crime, transgression, and pain are firmly embedded in the patriarchal order of things.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: There was an elephant living in my house, but all the adults were avoiding it. The elephant kept changing its shape and grew up with me. A story about the discovery of one’s own sexuality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: A former couple meet again at a railway station. Familiarity flares up, turning into an animalistic chaos of lust and desire.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Bubbly Delight)

films.syn: Forcefully drawn, the brutal autobiographical tale from Charles Bukowski shows how violence is answered by violence and passed down from generation to generation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: A man with spikes on his head lives in a surreal world at the top of a tower. This experimental video, shot on 16mm film, is a hybrid stop motion/live action film classic, combining dusty timelessness, theatrical violence and Cold Wave ambient styles.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: In a farmhouse a woman tries to lure the mischievous resident house spirit with offerings of food. During the night, as ghosts move through the house, he slips into the woman’s dream. But something has changed – spring has arrived.
A war has been settled down, but a conflict against each other is still escalating…
When Young-seok is taking his mother to the hospital, a truck suddenly appears. He turns the steering wheel and the world stops at that moment. What will happen next?

The story of a high school student whose best friend is faced with pregnancy. Director Jeong Hae-ji processes her personal experience with a close friend, delving into the topic of teen pregnancy and its consequences.
When Suzume accidentally frees a mysterious cat, she triggers a series of events that threatens all of Japan. Will it be possible to restore the old order?

At swim practice, a girl is confronted with her changing body while being bombarded by the whistling of her eccentric coach, the burden of God’s watchful eye, the majesty of the older swimmers and naughty recordings on her teammate’s mobile phone.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Camping on the Ocean Floor)

films.syn: An abstract pool where everyone gets lost in their own thoughts. The atmospheric cut-out animation combines an array of materials with varied and unique results.

ap.p: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Meet me by the Pool)

films.syn: By means of an embroidery, a Tapir mother reveals the story of her tragedy. She experienced a violent attack, the loss of her home and the disappearance of her son. Will she find him? “Tapir Memories” is based on real events about the impact of the armed conflict in Colombia in the early 2000s.

Standing alone in an elegant room, a famous Russian composer reflects on the significant encounters of his life as well as his musical achievements. A myriad of sights and sounds finally leaves him satisfied with his fate.

In her poetic, hand-drawn animated film, Liu Wan-Ling tells the story of a watchman who works in a major city. Among the skyscrapers, he discovers a small piece of undeveloped wilderness and encounters a little egret during his visits there. A heartfelt relationship develops between man and nature that outlasts even the destructive work of approaching construction equipment.

In his second feature-length film “La fôret de Mademoiselle Tang”, French-Cambodian director Denis Do provides us with touching insight into the Chinese society, thereby enabling us to better understand its recent history. The film is accompanied by a magnificent film score composed by Thibault Kientz-Agyeman, who also integrated traditional Chinese instruments such as the erhu into the soundtrack. Do and Kientz-Agyeman had already collaborated on the director’s successful debut film “Funan”, which dazzled audiences at Fantoche in 2018 and won the Cristal for Best Feature Film at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival. (Xenia Nguyen)
A gift brings joy; but sometimes, recipients can react unexpectedly. An ultra-short and funny claymation film from the UK.

The story of a young social worker caring for elderly people with dementia at a retirement home. Short and bittersweet, the film is a look into the lives of people suffering from dementia, and their feelings of alienation and slowly fading out of a world they once used to know.

Eccentric inventor Leonardo Da Vinci teams up with the Princess Marguerite to unravel the mysteries of the universe. An ode to human creativity with a captivating blend of stop motion and hand-drawn animation.
Forty-year-old Irma goes on a vacation to an all-inclusive resort. Soon after her arrival, she realises the site is meant for young families. Irma has to find her own place in this holiday paradise.

A poor man out stealing imagines how it might feel to be rich. Would he be a better person than the wealthy farmer he’s stealing from? This Hungarian cartoon takes a humorous look at the corrupting nature of money and power.

An unemployed cellist, a fallen rock star and a ruthless animal trainer compete on the street for the attention of passersby and a few coins. Stray dog Pirat livens up these unlikely fellow travellers in misfortune. A heartwarming cartoon from Russia.

Two characters become victims of circumstance at a de-militarised border as a boy looks after his traumatised father. Individuals in this film are manipulated by the political powers that lead characters to extremes.
This is a vivid story of Wa-bull (“lying Buddha”) in the Unjusa Temple, Hwasun County, in South Joella (Jeollanam-do) Province in South Korea.
Something is wrong with Bean-TOBO’s insides. This tale of friendship, loss and mental health is set in a dream-state universe that turns out not to be too different from our own.

Humankind no longer exists; only Fluor and Carlix, two ghosts in sportswear, remain. They wander among the remains of an extinct civilization, one in search of a Wi-Fi connection, the other searching for a giant whale’s head – a story of encounter and friendship.

At the mercy of the dentist’s chair, the protagonist cannot escape a confrontation with pain and the dregs of the miserable human condition. To distract himself, he takes refuge in a fantasised story of fishermen and the sea.
Not far from the quaint little town of Cardamom live the three robbers Casper, Jasper and Jonathan. They frequently sneak into town at night to break into the butcher’s shop or rob the bakery.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: The journey of the airship Norge to the North Pole ranks among the most important feats of the early 20th century. In her feature film debut, Norwegian director Kajsa Næss captures this flight in compelling images, frequently incorporating real archival footage to underscore the historical reality of the event. Despite the epic background, “Titina” excels first and foremost as a quiet study of two solitary people who are as ingenious as they are eccentric and whose friendship is in danger of breaking apart due to stubbornness and historical circumstances. (Mischa Haberthür)

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Bubbly Delight)

films.t: Tony, Shelly and the Magic Light
films.syn: Eleven-year-old Tony was born with an unusual feature: he glows. He spends his days at home in his blanket fort and dreams of no longer being alone. His world is soon turned upside down though when a peculiar girl named Shelly moves in.

The growth and decay of a field full of sunflowers, told as a parable of political conformity and dissidence. The consequences of collectivism and individualism are presented in a fun and child-friendly way in this French cartoon.

A shoal of herrings, adopting fantastic formations, roams the vast ocean. When seagulls suddenly attack, one small herring finds itself stranded in a tidal pool. As it searches desperately for a way out, it discovers many other sea creatures here. And now there is no time for fear: only by joining forces can they hope to defend themselves against the hungry seagull.

A young woman comes across animations on the internet that have clearly been created from her private selfies. An unknown woman with the same name confesses to identity theft. But death is quicker than the answer to the question: “Why?”

In a run-down neighbourhood, Zoe and her little brother Theo are left to fend for themselves. A young adolescent, Zoe is a ball of anger haunted by an intimate terror. Theo, still a child, flees reality into a fantastical world. During a scorching summer day, the two children will have to burst the abscess of their relationship so as not to lose each other.
On a beautiful summer night, a group of animals decide to avenge the death of one of their own.

Two very different teddy-bear brothers go unicorn hunting. This dark tale may seem familiar to those who caught the feature film “Unicorn Wars” at Fantoche 2022. In 2013, Alberto Vazquez sketched out the story in light pencil drawings and watercolours in the short film it was based on.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: From a drain in a bathtub a woman encounters love at first sight and a series of important choices. As the water rises, her thoughts begin to race, and two options present themselves – sink or swim. This hand-drawn, stop-motion piece in stark black-and-white reveals the artist at her unruly best.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: The voice of a cosmonaut re-entering Earth’s atmosphere and dying was accidentally recorded in 1961. This nameless heroine of space and imagination was obliterated from the history of the Soviet space programme. This unique film, pulsating with colour, brings her back into the herstory of the space race.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: After a particularly stimulating massage, a client in a spa seeks to seduce her masseur. A sensual and playful game unfolds in a maze of bodies, emotions and vapours in almost hypnotic 3D animation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno Popolare: Bubbly Delight)

films.syn: The contents hidden in this chest spark many people’s imaginations. The chest travels a long way around the world, through different countries, before we catch sight of what’s inside.

films.t: What's Love Got To Do With It – Miles Davis

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: Leading a peaceful life at home, protected from any kind of information – that’s the goal of the main character in this fascinating Czech stop-motion film made entirely from origami. Can this kind of project succeed?

The sun and moon take it in turns to rise above a stunning landscape. But what do the people think they’re doing? This Spanish stop-motion film illustrates the consequences of careless treatment of the environment and shows some ways out of the crisis.

Budapest in the year 2123: the world has become nearly uninhabitable; plants and animals are extinct. The city can only survive thanks to the great sacrifice made by its inhabitants: at the age of 50, people’s bodies become the property of the community and are used as a source of nourishment and oxygen.

A man has disappeared. Who was he? What drove him? What happened to him? In the style of a raw and sketchy mockumentary, the film lets people speak who seem to have known him. Will they find answers to their questions?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: Mixing hand drawings, cut-outs, and collage, this film allegorically speaks of the fate of economic migrants in Europe, the continent of opportunities.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Punk Is Not Dead)

films.syn: A wolf who is a novelist comes to a serene countryside retreat to write a masterpiece. One rainy day, a lady visits him with six-year-old Young-hee, and says “Young-hee, this wolf is your father.” This is the story of how the wolf-novelist becomes the father of a little girl.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 8)

films.syn: An empty paper depicts a struggle between artistic composition and decomposition as the voice of the narrator-protagonist reminisces about her tumultuous relationship with a former girlfriend.
The story of Eli the Eagle, who ends up raising a baby penguin. Will he manage to make the little penguin fly?

The beloved young countess escapes the bullying of her jealous step-family with a little unexpected help. Lovingly restored, this Spanish take on Cinderella is a must for fans of fairytales, featuring a nostalgic animation style and a few clever surprises here and there.

In 1993, Scotty moves with his family to the bourgeois industrial city of Edmonton. His strict father, a policeman, is determined to impose his values on his teenage son, but there is only one passion in life for Scotty: punk rock!
What would happen if intelligent machines started developing their own goals, different from those of humankind?

films.t: A Dream From Last Night (Healing Water)
films.syn: In this brief, yet rich animation, as two figures face each other in the water, reality itself becomes fluid, like a dream.

ap.p: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water)

films.syn: Situations and stories from the lives of cows: cows grazing in the pasture, cows bringing peace to people in a therapy garden, cows in the slaughterhouse... A patchwork of idyllic and dramatic images illustrates the connection between humans and animals in both a positive and negative light and ends by giving us hope for a better world.

Abubilla is the name of the bird in the starring role of this Spanish stop motion film. We follow him to the rhythm of a song as he fights against the consequences of the destruction of his habitat. Can he do something to stop the deforestation?
A person brushes the teeth of a dog and turns into a bus.

Through water, a Chinese manicurist in Miami nurtures, cleans and caresses her clients, while attempting to describe feelings she doesn't yet have the words for. As people drift away from each other, water becomes a source of comfort in a drought pervaded by solitude.

ap.p: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water)

films.syn: Howling werewolves, the full moon like a disc. All the space collapses in on itself and puts itself back together. Loss of control and a state of uncertainty. A space walk through planetary conflict zones. It’s not just on earth that things are blowing up in people’s faces.
Vigo is meant to meet Camille in the cinema. He finds the wait stressful and one friend shows up unexpectadly.
A fish swims through an empty city, it dies and it is reborn; as time cannot slow down, all this animated fish can do is keep swimming.

ap.p: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water)

films.syn: Marmar listens to the stories told by her grandmother’s friends as they play an illicit game of cards. Based on childhood memories and shared stories, this film is a tale of love, grief and resilience. At its heart, it is a tribute to the solidarity of Iranian women.

The expanse of the ocean extends bleak, dark, sparkling across the screen. Yelling, stuttering images. Distortions and shifts destabilise perception. With threatening dynamics and violent clamping force flowing through it, an abyss appears on the impenetrable surface of the water.
Inspired by Puccini’s opera Madame Butterfly, this exquisite stop-motion film by Canadian director Pjotr Sapegin relates the eternal and heartbreaking tale of unrequited love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: An ode to the laundry basket. The object becomes a vortex, a black hole, whose end seems to be getting closer but is never reached, meaning the ground always remains out of sight. Everyday life becomes transcendental. A cyclical dance, a circular battle, a lyrical experiment.
Three balding brothers travel to Istanbul to get a hair transplant. Stuck with each other in a hotel far from home, their insecurities grow faster than their hair.

A man lives alone in a block of flats. He may not be able to put a finger on it but he is lonely. All this changes though when the odd growth he has been ignoring on his side turns out to be something alive and becomes conscious.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: Artists call it “hand memory”: knowledge that isn’t stored in the brain, but in the body and is activated when you start painting, sculpting or drawing. Şirin Bahar Demirel wonders which memories are passed on through the hands and whether we can read the aggressive nature of a painter from their brushwork, or the desires of a textile artist from their embroidery.

While still asleep, a woman is dragged from her house by a huge black mass. She is taken to a group of women and girls who behave like a herd of untamed cows. The woman spends the night imitating this behaviour. When the group merges, the mass moves back to town to take a new woman at nightfall.

Various figures live in their boxes in a controlled system. Day after day, they go about their work until an imbalance causes the system to falter and collapse. Through the collapse, the characters find each other and discover life outside the boxes together.
A young woman recalls the day when she was attacked by three men on her way home. But daily life must resume its course.
You can be lonely even when you’re surrounded by people. This Chinese cartoon sensitively broaches the topic of connection from the perspective of a young girl seeking contact with her mother.
A dissatisfying marriage, a secret crush, and workplace fantasies come to a head in a diner run by a mole with a hot ass.

Bobby loves her mum. Their relationship is unbreakable or so she thinks. When she is surprised by a last-minute trip to the hospital, an innocent check-up soon turns into a twisted lie. As she tries to escape this deranged nightmare, she realises that there is only one person to blame for all of this … mum.

films.t: Busby Berkeley's Tribute to Mae West
films.syn: Hollywood’s most famous choreographer meets one of her most famous quotes: “Is that a gun in your pocket?”
A community of garden creatures all contribute to the flow of life, using water from a fountain. When a butterfly gets stuck in the fountain, they’re faced with an unfamiliar situation.

Vladimir and Olga raise ducks on a small farm in the countryside. A wounded duck awakens motherly feelings in Olga. The couple are hoping for a child, but this expectation soon turns into a nightmare. A stop-motion horror runs its course.

In eight movements inspired and accompanied by the music of Camille Saint-Saëns, this animated short film is a mini-symphony of sexual fantasy. These animated musical vignettes show many facets of erotic love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: A mother and son navigate their lust and loneliness in the queerest of ways.

A circular water wheel in a stream meets a strobe light. In 35 mm, two cameras capture the movement and stillness with and against time. A double trick that poetically shakes perception and plays with the boundaries between illusion and reality.

In this Kyrgyz film, the daughter of a hunter and a young wolf are looking for their parents. When they find them, they face a difficult decision. The film poetically questions the possibility of peace against a backdrop of intergenerational conflicts.

On 11 & 12 February 2006 at the ski resort of Klewenalp the portraits of Swiss men, women and children are captured with a time lapse camera. Inhabitants of central Switzerland head for the mountains, arrive in cars, trains, boats and buses, queue for the cable car, and then ski, snowboard, toboggan, eat, drink and fall asleep.

This film explains the myth behind the creation of our planet. Two gods create the world and complement one another perfectly – until humankind is born. An atmospheric and profound film about mutual respect and tolerance of all living beings.
A girl draws a circle on the ground. Passersby step into it, one by one. Soon the circle is full of people, struggling to stay within.
A squid has a new record – but instead of celebrating with other music fans, he wants to keep the music to himself. Can the other animals convince him that music is best listened to as a group?

films.t: Cold In The Mourning – Tamara Qaddoumi

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: A girl dreams of the sea, which is so close and yet unreachable. Several years later, she takes us to an enchanted underwater world that she has managed to get to. This serene stop motion film is made using paper.

Like folded ink blot images, pictures are reflected over their axis and form a kaleidoscope of ecstatic bodies and lustful frolics. New scope for interpretation appears upside down, reversed, mirror inverted and negatively inverted: “Open up your eyes now, tell me what you see.”

Dieter, an ill sculptor, hasn’t really been able to work for a long time. Simple tasks elude him. His thoughts frequently transport him away from his workshop into another, fantastic world, into mysterious landscapes.
Are you looking for a place to stay? Diva Sicanella is pleased to give you a tour of her manor. Reviews (1): Location: 5/5 Cleanliness: 5/5 Friendliness: 5/5 Overall impression: 5/5

Flickering behind the eyes, voices between derailment and control. The idea of “don’t know what” is dissected and turned upside down. Image by image, the manipulation causes alienation. Jittering and pausing, everything is precisely garbled; the voice becomes music, the body an instrument.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: The camera suffers from a psychosis similar to human schizophrenia; this disorder subtly alters every single frame of the film, while the narrative remains superficially intact. A reworking of the 1941 classic “Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde”, in which the actors are replaced in every single frame.

Sam has been worrying about their identity. One night, Sam is visited by an urban fox who leads Sam to the attic and gives a flamboyant musical performance. But Sam wants more than just a show. A beguiling animated puppet film that calls for solidarity.

Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, many Russians have shared dreams about their president on social media. A selection of these posts has been brought to life in this film. The result is a bizarre and disturbing nightmare vision that explores the theme of the collective unconscious in Russian society.

Inbetween reality and memory, at Dürrenwaid 8, in a house near a stream, the present, the past, and the future emerge as one and the same, as family history, childhood memories, stories and observations come together in this experimental Heimatfilm.

ap.p: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water)

films.syn: ECHOES is a brief animated journey, conceived as a personal diary of the past two years. Drawing inspiration from real, visited places, it unfolds as an unscripted, non-narrative sequence of animated sketches.

A hand-drawn film about hair, dysphoria, and the growing pains of a repeating puberty. It follows the titular tall child as they outgrow their tiny apartment, their gender, and their hallucinatory giant ground sloth Edith.

films.t: Embodied Structures - Come Feel My Skins
films.syn: Movements through dark silvery waters, from darkness into a glossy space. Islands of fleshy sculptural figures and sleek surfaces that fold into skins. Beyond the binary between the organic and artificial, the digital and physical, speculative bodies grant access to magical realities. (Comissioned by CIVA / sound:frame)
On planet Banana, no one seems to be worried about the future. In very little time, this stop motion film reflects on the topic of consumerism and the consequences for the environment.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Ciné–Concert: Georges & Louis Schwizgebel)

films.t: Ernest & Célestine – Le voyage en Charabie
films.syn: After their first Oscar-nominated adventure, Ernest the bear and Célestine the mouse are back! When Ernest’s violin is accidentally broken, only the violin maker in Gibberitia can repair it. But Gibberitia has changed a lot: all musical notes have been banned, apart from the note of C.

A poem and a cup of black coffee. Everything is floating. A dream, magic, a chain reaction – this creates a cycle beyond formalised reality. Illusion and uncertainty. A new world forms away from the familiar regime.
The hunger of a lab snail makes it the unexpected heroine of huge adventures. This Russian film shows that even small creatures can sometimes have a big impact.

It’s often the small things you remember best: the feeling of raindrops on your skin or the sand between your toes. In this poetic Irish film, we delve into the childhood memories of an adult on a camping weekend with their father and sister.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Kurzfilme in der Kirche)

films.syn: Grand gestures, determined expressions and sturdy legs. Roughly collaged footballers owe each other nothing and a referee loses his vision. Caution: Not really for football fans.

Humans live their daily lives a seemingly mechanical world whose various parts work with a common rhythm. But then something unexpected comes from outside and throws a spanner in the works. What happens if one of the parts falls out of sync?
The story of a grandfather’s perilous swim from China to Hong Kong parallels his granddaughter’s own quest for a new freedom.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Retrospective: Sacrebleu Productions – Women Only)

films.syn: A playful philosophical piece, inspired by a Wittgenstein quotation: “What prevents me from supposing that this table either vanishes or alters its shape when no one is observing it and then when someone looks at it again changes back? But one feels like saying - who is going to suppose such a thing?”

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: A fleeting encounter between Touch and Long Swipe becomes an algorithmic love story. Distortions appear: a breakdown of the image, an aberration in the story. While hands and objects move in continuous circles, surprisingly sensory tales emerge outside the orbit.

Without warning, stubborn Karin suddenly finds herself back in the care of her grandfather. To find her parents, she must join forces with a rude cat. This Japanese- French co-production was partly filmed in live action and then rotoscoped in a creative way.
From the tormented little mermaid to the fulfilled woman she is today, Gigi tells us about her gender transition with humor and sensitivity.

films.t: Grandma’s Recipe – Renan Inquérito e Liah Vitória

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: The screen is a vibrating membrane, spitting out and swallowing colours, shapes and noisy sounds. Psychedelic colours and suction, a sensory whirlpool of happiness suspends everything external, with hypnotic circles imploding and intense sounds bursting on a pleasant trip.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: An exclusive behind-the-scenes look at the making of The Boy and the Heron over seven years, with unique access to Studio Ghibli.
A fisher girl loses her beloved boat in a storm. But something new can always emerge from a loss.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno I: Waves of Change)

films.syn: Only yesterday, dragons were coming down to see what humans were doing in their valleys. Destroying everything in their path, we cursed them, in vain.
A piglet discovers the joy of ice skating and wants to show it to his friend Cow. This affectionate stop motion film animated with puppets brings us closer to accepting ourselves just the way we are.
“I Am Here” explores the need to imprint ourselves onto the world and build a legacy.

24 February 2022 my boyfriend and I fled from Kyiv to Irpin. We spent 10 days in a blockaded city and managed to escape with the last evacuation convoy. Time passed, but the feeling that I died in Irpin never left me since then. The film reconstructs this true story of survival through a personal and subjective lens.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.t: I Would Eat if I Could
films.syn: Marci bursts into her former residence, into the peaceful rural environment, on a crowded subway train. His friends welcome him and they go to their favorite place. On the way, it quickly becomes clear that Marci cannot settle back into the old idyll. He keeps wandering off and on.

Cloudscapes, billowing shapes in their outlines. Political speech acts tell of violence and excessive demand. Landscapes are reflected, upside down. Empty phrases uttered about people on the move. About escape. The vocabulary skews the perception. Over 3,000 frames, celestial bodies and experiences illustrate the gulf between narrative and experience.
On this short journey from big to small, you can get quite dizzy. This animated film from the USA adopts an amusing approach to showing us that there are different views of reality.
A young otter considers three mossy stones to be his family. In the otter’s imagination, they spend a wonderful time together. But at some point, their true nature can no longer be ignored.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno I: Waves of Change)

films.syn: An animated animal couple tries to resolve their problems.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: Motion study and restless exploration. How do you achieve an undefined goal? Signs from the outside world – they unmistakably and unequivocally take everything in. Internally it remains coded and inconsistent. A question of choice or circumstances?
A puffer fish keeps being disturbed while playing peacefully. But he has a strategy to drive away the troublemakers. A funny film on the topic of anxiety and how we can deal with it.

That very night, houses will burn. Men and women will tremble. Hordes of children will come together and howl as they dance alone on the ashes like wild bears. It only takes one shout to wake them all from their slumber!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Retrospective: Sacrebleu Productions – Women Only)

films.syn: A furry tongue. Who is the beautiful beast? Fantastical speculations about the internal and external. Surreal arrays and fluffy surfaces conjure up physical sensations. Cosy dream worlds and eerie objects evade inspection and promote liberation.
In a woman’s room, memories constantly accumulate and disappear like dust. A man spends his time in this room, creating futile little games with the woman’s memories.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Retrospective: Sacrebleu Productions – Women Only)
Officially selected (section: Ciné–Concert: Georges & Louis Schwizgebel)

films.t: La jeune fille et les nuages

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Ciné–Concert: Georges & Louis Schwizgebel)

films.syn: Breasts plump, bum tight, plumage smooth. She’s ready for her date. But her daughter clings onto her – she doesn’t want her to go. Very soon, however, this fledgling pubescent will give in to her sexual desire and experience disappointment. In the conflict-ridden world the two women inhabit, men evade partnership and fatherhood. The family dog is her only support.

aw: Special Mention Swiss Competition Youth Jury

films.syn: In the depths of winter, a woman finds a baby in a forest and takes it in against the wishes of her husband. In this emotional adaptation of a novel, directed by Michel Hazanavicius (“The Artist”), life in an ancient fairly-tale forest provides a sharp contrast to the horrors of the Holocaust.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: A girl is with her younger brother on the beach and falls head over heels for a boy who seems to have no fear. It takes all her courage to win his heart. A computer-animated 3D film that plays with stereotypes of seduction.

It’s Sunday. At lunch, James observes his family. They ask him questions, but don’t listen to his answers; they give him advice which they don’t follow themselves. They caress him, they smack him. It is just an ordinary Sunday lunch.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Retrospective: Sacrebleu Productions – Women Only)

films.syn: A young dragon arrives in a human town looking for a new home. Little does he know that this is easier said than done.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno I: Waves of Change)

films.syn: What brews within, emotions, desires, and pain need to flow free like water through a stream; it is a strong, deep, organic feeling, a knot of emotions and feelings so real, and yet so difficult to convey. When words fail, images take over.

ap.p: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno II: A Fish out of Water)

films.syn: Coco is 6. She lives in a big house with her mother and aunt. One night, she wakes with a start after a terrible nightmare about a character resembling Woody Woodpecker. She asks her mom to call the police.

Bodies and two-dimensional images fold into one another, achieving unexpected depth in the zooming in, in the pixelation. A sensual choreography of desires emerges from the manipulation. A blown tyre, shortness of breath and deep sighing. A reappropriation of lesbian pornography. A photo love story, poster sex.

Ben loves to cook and eat. But when he hits puberty, his appearance suddenly becomes important, his weight becomes a problem and he is bullied by other kids. For Ben and his friends, their journey of self-acceptance and companionship begins – and it’s not always easy.
A fly flies to see a close friend.

A young woman starts a long-distance relationship. She feels lonely and lost in her new situation and tries to get in touch with her partner. Her feelings oscillate between melancholy, frustration, hope and excitement.

Fujion and Kyomoto are complete opposites, but they find each other through their shared love of manga. Then something happens that neither of them ever expected. At Annecy this anime, which was produced by just a small team, went from insider secret to public favourite just by word of mouth.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Ciné–Concert: Georges & Louis Schwizgebel)

films.syn: Leipzig, 1989. Margarethe, a young punk who rebels against the East German regime, is in a psychiatric clinic. She dreams of breaking out and going to the man she loves, the punk musician Heinrich. Although the regime's days may be numbered, the Stasi spies are more present than ever.

Yellow and red lines infiltrate the landscape. Forests, fields and coastlines are dissected, filleted and divided into a geometric grid. Ever faster, to the rhythm of the music. Rumours on land. Market Sentiments sketches out the violent fragmentation of the world.

An old silent film from the 1910s, rediscovered and restored, tells the story of the passenger pigeon, the once most abundant bird on earth, wiped out in just a few decades by mankind. The film is enriched by the audio testimony of the last passenger pigeon: Martha.
Tony is the ultimate good guy. He takes the smallest piece of the cake, helps strangers who have lost their way in the city – in short, his kindness knows no limits. He also lives with an angel.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: In a dystopian world where people are forbidden to touch one another, Matta and Matto offer a place of refuge for the lonely in their travelling hotel. In the rooms of the Hotel Vaip, the guests’ find their deepest desires fulfilled and even surpassed. But this comes at a high price.
Two pieces of meat fall in love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: The film questions solitude, misunderstanding and disunity. Everything happening to the characters is not a true love yet. Everybody finds their way to be unhappy. Everybody is looking for love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: Flip book and disobedient horses. The essence of cinematic illusion is investigated in a series of four episodes. Everyday objects, bodies and time are in constant motion. The head slams against the wall and the machines are constantly, magically recalibrated.

When writer Joe R. Ackerley rescues a young German Shepherd, he has no idea that he has found the love of his life in her. Warm-hearted and melancholy, featuring British humour and sketchy drawings, “My Dog Tulip” recounts the highs and lows in the everyday life of this unlikely couple.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)
Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: Layers of newspaper, mouths and nylon peel away in sync with a heartbeat. A face sheds its skin rebelliously. Distorted grimaces twist and turn through holes – openings to the outside. At the end it feels like there has been an act of liberation. It’s much more than fabric that’s being torn open here.
In this film, cars have legs. Maybe that is why they feel free to use the pavement as they please. There is no room, but could we perhaps be a little more considerate?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: Simone Massi’s first feature film weaves together the personal stories, memories and dreams of three children from different generations. With the help of some wellknown literary quotes and his distinctive scratch technique, Massi paints a dark, pulsating portrait of 20th century Italy.
A nun digs a man up from the ground and loses her grip on everyday life. Can secrets and harmony coexist?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Kurzfilme in der Kirche)

films.syn: A young woman is stuck in the queue of a telephone hotline. A surreal, episodic short film about the absurdities of urban life and the feeling of paralysing stagnation.

aw: Special Mention Swiss Competition Swiss Jury

films.syn: 350 million years ago, an underwater isopod involuntarily takes its first steps on land – and discovers an adventurous new habitat.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno I: Waves of Change)

films.syn: Six-year-old Lily visits her grandmother, who has had a mastectomy and now misses her breasts. When Lily finds out that her grandmother’s shadow still has both breasts, she is prepared to do anything to get them back.

When the Hungarian borders open in 1989, three friends come up with a clever plan to get their hands on the unaffordable train tickets they need to travel. A mix of documentary-style interviews and reenactments show viewers how a whole generation got the opportunity to discover the world.

With the sea and the urban Algarve as a background, we follow a complete cycle of the life of a special shellfish called percebes, goose barnacle. From their formation to the dish, in this journey, we cross different contexts that allow us to better understand this region and those who live there.
When pixels do themselves some good.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: All we need is love)

films.syn: The anthropomorphic princess Sophie and her maid Jessica prepare for a new day in the royal court. Sophie’s struggle to play her role propels the two protagonists forward and backward in time, through worlds and identities, to find a way to live together.
A magician is preparing a dangerous illusion – will it go well? This funny stop motion film made using plasticine allows us to experience the thrills.

The body misses space, taking stock of relationships. An orbit described through the camera. The perspective is shifted, the field of view is splintered. The artist in her living space, the living space upside down. Is living working? Is filming living?

The film explores the question of what makes humans human in the age of technology and artificial intelligence. Using a unique 3D animation technique, Swiss artist Yves Netzhammer takes an unsparing look at the present and future of the digital age in his feature-film debut and reflects on the reciprocal condition of human and non-human beings in a constant cycle of becoming and passing away.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Ciné–Concert: Georges & Louis Schwizgebel)

films.syn: Based on the “Tibetan Book of the Dead”, living creatures are meeting dead ones: O Nobly-Born, your breathing is about to cease. Listen with full attention, without being distracted. O Nobly-Born, go forward, you have been in a swoon.

Dan spends a lot of time in his flat. His daily life is accompanied by the electronic music pumping through his headphones. But when the young man goes outside, he feels disconnected from the world around him and only finds solace in nightclubs. One day, he catches the eye of a baby who will change his perception of the world around him.

Eight years after “Ma vie de Courgette” (My Life as a Zucchini), Claude Barras returns with a plea against the destruction of nature. This scrupulous stop motion film is about a young girl that rescues an orphaned baby orangutan from the edge of a palm oil plantation and gets caught between two sides.

Skin as surface, as material, as landscape. Slow movements through changing terrain, wrinkled ravines and flat expanses. New and mysterious structures keep appearing until the image itself becomes porous and the focus disappears.

A moving painting of physical sensations. Maria Lassnig in an animated self-portrait, a musical. Revolving around her own head. Idols and projections; Garbo, mother, woman. Becoming a different person, circling around herself. Trying herself out, trying herself on, finding outlines to redraw herself while singing.

Feelings, musings and dreams teeter in the dozy state between sleep and wakefulness. They form delirium. A wolf howls outside – or is it a whale? – while the moon scurries by and bares its teeth. Alongside the befriended Epson printer, the body floats through the starry sky.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.t: Sirocco et le royaume des courants d'air
films.syn: Sisters Juliette and Carmen accidentally fall into the magical world of their favourite book. But how will they get back home? They will have to be creative and work together. Much of this beautifully drawn family film portrays a childlike logic.

After the Second World War, eleven-year-old François leads a sheltered life with his parents in a Parisian suburb. While he is very close to his mother, his taciturn and distant father remains a great mystery to him. One day, his parents start building a wooden sailing boat in the garden.

A tangle of whispering, murmuring voices becomes a polyphonic love poem. Tongues flick, smack and roll in moist, soft, crude sounds. A being, sometimes tongue, sometimes slug, against a hairy background.

Under a scorching sun, Charlie is bored and dreams of going to the seaside. But she's forced to stay in a dingy motel with her cousin Jess, who slouches in her deckchair. The pool is empty, the sun is beating down and the tension is mounting: the ecological apocalypse announced on the radio suddenly becomes real.

As sleep arrives, a little monkey glides gently from one leaf to another in a mysterious dream world. What will he come across? A film that takes us on a journey through the various stages and forms of sleep.

Visitors to the park often leave behind crumbs from their picnic – but the sparrows in this film aren’t satisfied with leftovers. This amusing computer-animated film poses the question of whether sparrows actually are sparrowbrains.

An assembly of endless reflections. Thoughts. No beginning, no end. Amorphous shapes contract and expand. Colours and concrete lines on vague surfaces, hinting at endless spaces. Two gestures in ink and pencil.
When a starry-eyed duckling stumbles upon a strange portal, he journeys into unfamiliar worlds, not knowing if he’ll make it back home.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Bagno I: Waves of Change)

films.syn: The commotion begins when someone accidentally damages a statue that everyone respects. Whether their respect for the statue was sincere or a forced belief began to be revealed through the destruction of the statue.

A radical reworking of an etching by the Italian artist Giorgio Morandi, brought to life by engraving frame by frame directly into the photographic emulsion of colour filmstock. The viewer is taken on a journey through the etching, accompanied by the sounds that the artist might have heard from his window as he worked.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: Deeper and deeper into unknown waters. Bubbles rise between thick algae and insect legs. An abysmal habitat, mysterious noises and creepy movements, the occasional ray of sunlight. The surface of the water becomes the bottom of the lake, surfacing and submerging, crossing parallel universes.

The film tells the story of Inés, an animation artist from Spain, who stumbles across the book “Sultana’s Dream” while in India. She is fascinated by the book because it describes a matriarchal utopia at the beginning of the 20th century, in which women rule a peaceful and safe country while the men have to stay at home. Inés embarks on a journey to find the location of this utopia and in doing so, unleashes her own dreams.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Music Video Darlings Vol. 9)

films.syn: In the black shimmering of the picture, blurry images flash for fractions of a second, while in the center a swirling, growing something struggles to take shape. A study in cinematic abstraction, anchored in a night ride on Vienna’s public transportation system

Hybrid organisms break away from the idea of a physical entity. Rigid boundaries become permeable, membranes expand, mutate, are crossed, penetrated. A complex network in constant flux proves that bodies, as Donna Haraway says, don’t end at the skin.

Can we tell our mother that we have been sexually assaulted by our brother? The obvious answer should be “yes”. However, only few dare to break the silence. The question we ask ourselves is: “Why aren’t we talking about it?”

Mr. Ham decides to have his heart removed to free himself from his complicated emotions. The doctor assures him that, in this day and age, this procedure presents no problem. Of a pensive disposition, Mr. Ham keeps his heart for a while after the removal in the hope of understanding it better someday.

Juanjo and Miquel have barely anything in common. But they soon become friends through their shared love of heavy metal. Using charming observations and minimalist images, this humorous coming-of-age story follows the boys on a nostalgic journey of growing up.
A robotic vacuum suffering from burnout quits its job at a hospital and sets out to find community and a greater purpose on a quiet street where two lonely rabbits are stuck in perpetual loops.

A ship sets sail on an epic voyage through malignant natural and supernatural elements from which one man alone survives. An adaptation of Coleridge’s “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner”, illustrated by19th Century wood engravings which are animated by scratching directly into the surface of color filmstock.

In his last (for now) feature film, Hayao Miyazaki draws on personal childhood experiences, motifs from the pacifist children’s book “How Do You Live?” and his relationship with his long-time companions to create this thoughtful and imaginative look back at his career.

films.t: The Car That Came Back From the Sea
films.syn: Full of exuberance and frivolousness, six friends drive to the Polish Baltic coast and back in a small, beaten-up car. During their trip, their car and their country fall apart. Nevertheless, life goes on.

aw: Special Mention Swiss Competition Youth Jury
